n: Wine and strong drink are pictured as people: one mocks, the other brawls. Anyone led astray by them is not wise. Latter-day Saints see this principle carried further in the Word of Wisdom.
A king’s fury is like a lion’s roar; whoever provokes him risks his own life.

f.g: The terror a king inspires; his wrath.

n: It is honorable to avoid a fight; only fools are quick to quarrel.

f.g: Quick to break out in a quarrel.

n: The lazy farmer won’t plow in the chilly autumn, so at harvest he looks for a crop and finds nothing.

f.g: Plowing happened in autumn, at the start of the rainy season.

n: A person’s real purposes lie deep like water in a well, but a discerning person can draw them out—a good description of a wise counselor or listener.

f.g: Like drawing water up from a deep well.

n: Many people claim to be loyal and good, but a truly faithful person is hard to find.

f.w: a faithful man who can find?

n: The righteous live with integrity, and their children are blessed after them. Good character becomes a family legacy.

f.w: his children are blessed after him

n: A king on his judgment seat sees through evil and scatters it, the way a farmer winnows chaff.
Who can honestly claim to have a perfectly clean heart, free from sin? No one—everyone needs God’s mercy.

f.w: I am pure from my sin

n: Using two sets of weights and measures—one for buying, one for selling—is detestable to the Lord.

f.g: divers = different, varying; a heavy weight for buying and a light one for selling.

n: Even children show their character by what they do—whether their conduct is pure and right.

f.w: Even a child is known by his doings

n: Ears that hear and eyes that see were both made by the Lord. He gave us these senses, and he himself sees and hears all.

f.w: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye

n: Don’t love sleep or you will grow poor; stay awake and you’ll have plenty of food.
A slice of market life: the buyer complains “It’s no good!” while haggling—then brags about his bargain afterward.
Gold and jewels are plentiful, but lips that speak knowledge are a rare treasure.
If someone foolishly guarantees a stranger’s debt, take his coat as collateral. He has shown he is a risk.

f.g: A cloak was taken as a pledge (collateral) for a loan.

n: Food gained by deceit tastes sweet at first, but later it’s like a mouthful of gravel.
Make plans by seeking advice; if you wage war, get guidance first.
A gossip betrays confidences, so avoid anyone who talks too much.

f.w: him that flattereth with his lips
f.g: Or “one who opens his lips wide”—a chatterer.

n: Whoever curses father or mother will have his lamp snuffed out in deep darkness. Under the law of Moses this was a capital offense.

f.w: Whoso curseth his father or his mother

f.g: Pitch-black darkness, like the middle of the night.

n: An inheritance grabbed too quickly at the beginning won’t be blessed in the end—like the prodigal son who demanded his share early.
Don’t say, “I’ll get even.” Wait for the Lord, and he will deliver you.
The Lord detests dishonest weights; rigged scales are not good. (Compare verse 10.)

f.w: a false balance is not good

n: The Lord directs a person’s steps; how then can anyone fully understand his own path? We see only part of the road.

f.w: Man's goings are of the LORD

n: It’s a trap to rashly dedicate something to God and only think it over later. Make vows carefully.

f.g: Rashly declares something holy, dedicating it to God.

n: A wise king sifts out the wicked like a farmer threshing grain by driving a wheel over it.

f.g: A threshing wheel or cart was rolled over grain to separate it from the husk.

n: The human spirit is like the Lord’s lamp, searching out a person’s innermost being. Latter-day Saints may think of the light of Christ given to everyone.

f.w: The spirit of man is the candle of the LORD

n: Loyal love and faithfulness protect a king; his throne is secured through love.

f.w: Mercy and truth preserve the king

n: Each age has its glory: young people have strength, and the old have the dignity of gray hair.
Blows that wound can scrub away evil; punishment can reach deep inside. Correction, though painful, can bring real change.

f.w: the inward parts of the belly
